audit.title: CCIP Move Module Interfaces Reference Documentation (Aptos)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Page opens with a title and a version list, not a self-contained answer. The best liftable line — "Initial release for the Aptos blockchain… Cross-chain messaging from Aptos to EVM-based chains" — is buried as a sub-bullet. Weak.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong for its size — 4 headings, 1 H1, max depth H3, 0 level skips, tidy bullets. No action needed on hierarchy.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Measured 0 numerals in prose; only `v1.6.0` present. Feature bullets ("Configurable gas limits", "native APT fee payments") lack any numbers, limits, or supported-chain lists. Weak.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 2 internal links, 0 external, 0 primary sources. No link to the CCIP concept page, the Aptos Move docs, or the CCIP spec. Weak.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: No one-sentence definition of "CCIP Move Module Interfaces" or what the Aptos integration provides. An engine has nothing crisp to lift. Weak.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Measured 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified. Head metadata could not be verified — CLI should pass raw `<head>`. On the served evidence, this is the lowest dimension.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code, expected for an index page — but even a minimal import/module-path reference or a link labeled as the entry module would help agents. Low lift here.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Answers "what versions exist" only. Misses "how do I use CCIP on Aptos", "does CCIP support Aptos token transfers", "what chains can Aptos send to". Weak.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; "CCIP", "Aptos", "EVM-based chains", "Fungible Assets" used consistently and unambiguously. No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a thin (100-word) version-index page whose only job is to route readers to the CCIP v1.6.0 Aptos API reference. Its biggest strength is clean, level-skip-free structure and unambiguous prose; its biggest weakness is that it carries almost no liftable substance — no definition of what CCIP-on-Aptos *is*, no metadata, no concrete parameters — so a generative engine landing here gets navigation, not an answer. As an index page this is acceptable UX but weak GEO: it should still contain one canonical, quotable definition and machine-readable metadata so it can be retrieved and cited for "what is CCIP on Aptos" style queries rather than being a dead-end pointer.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical, answer-first definition paragraph
recommendations.where: Immediately under the H1, before "## Available Versions".
recommendations.issue: Page opens with a version list; no self-contained statement of what this is.
recommendations.change: Add one lead sentence, e.g. "Chainlink CCIP on Aptos is a set of Move modules that enable cross-chain messaging and token transfers between Aptos and EVM-based chains, with native APT fee payments and configurable gas limits (current release: v1.6.0)."
recommendations.why: Gives engines a self-contained, verbatim-liftable answer to "what is CCIP on Aptos" — the query this URL should own.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/intent-phrased entry points
recommendations.where: Under "## Documentation Structure" or as short linked H3s.
recommendations.issue: Sections are concept-titled ("Router Functions", "Events"), not query-phrased.
recommendations.change: Phrase or annotate links as tasks: "Send a message from Aptos to an EVM chain", "Transfer tokens using Aptos Fungible Assets", "Handle CCIP errors on Aptos" — each linking into the v1.6.0 subpage.
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by task, not by concept name; task-phrased anchors win retrieval that concept titles lose.

recommendations.title: Add `TechArticle` JSON-LD, canonical URL, and last-updated
recommendations.issue: Measured 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` schema with `name`, `about: "Chainlink CCIP"`, `softwareVersion: "1.6.0"`, a canonical URL, and a visible "Last updated" line. Verify against raw `<head>` (not captured here).
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise agent trust and parse reliability (E-E-A-T).

recommendations.title: Add concrete specifics to the feature bullets
recommendations.issue: "Configurable gas limits and out-of-order execution" — no values or supported-chain names.
recommendations.change: Name the specific EVM chains supported for Aptos↔EVM, and state any gas-limit range or default; link the Fungible Asset standard.
recommendations.why: Quantitative/named specifics are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

recommendations.title: Add external/primary-source links
recommendations.change: Link "Move modules" to Aptos Move docs, "Fungible Assets" to the Aptos FA standard, and "CCIP" to the CCIP concept/overview page.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative links raise credibility and citation rate.

antiPatterns: Thin content: 100 words total, functioning as a pure pointer with no standalone answer.
Undated/unversioned metadata (no dateModified) — freshness signal absent.
No canonical URL and no JSON-LD in served HTML.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced from the page — good site-level signal; ensure this URL is listed in it.
Head metadata could not be verified from the provided content; pass raw `<head>` in the CLI for a full metadata read before treating schema/canonical as truly absent.
As an index page, some GEO weight legitimately lives on the linked v1.6.0 subpage; ensure that page carries the canonical definitions and code this landing page lacks.
